claims.statement: Execution, governance, lifecycle, and communication answer distinct authority questions.
claims.scope: A unit and interval under §4's definitions.
claims.caveat: These are proposed operational distinctions, not automatically observable from message traces.

claims.statement: Hive command reaches from a unique original root through the unit; fleet execution command is bounded by each node's local unit.
claims.caveat: Disjointness, node/unit coverage and connected coordination are additional fleet requirements.

claims.statement: A swarm's filtered command graph is edgeless; qualifying conferred, member-revocable, term-bounded leader edges are removed.
claims.caveat: An elected swarm may still use an operational dispatcher; E and D are different graphs.

claims.statement: The initial taxonomy has eight identified defects and permits multiple permanent dispatchers under its swarm rule.
claims.scope: Author's audit of his original proposal.
claims.caveat: This comparison does not prove the repair is the only coherent taxonomy.

claims.statement: Command, communication, ownership and lifecycle are logically separable through constructed contrasts.
claims.caveat: Logical separability does not establish statistical independence or lack of real-world correlation.

claims.statement: The initial rule agrees on 12 of 22 configurations, misclassifies 3 and cannot decide 7.
claims.caveat: Revised labels are the author's comparison target; no independent deployment census or full evidence recoding by this guide.

claims.statement: The selected published production LLM architectures are described as depth-1 hives.
claims.scope: Restricted to the configurations and architecture disclosures in Table 1.
claims.caveat: Do not generalise this observation to all production systems or every use of a framework.

claims.statement: All seven base structures report throughput 11.69 below saturation.
claims.scope: n=16, load 0.7, one-way latency 0.05, 200 seeds per condition.
claims.caveat: Arrival-limited equality is not equal maximum capacity or equal task quality.

claims.statement: Outage retention is HIVE 0.023 [0.022,0.024], FLEET 0.941 [0.933,0.950], elected swarm 0.996 [0.988,1.003].
claims.scope: 50-unit simulated outage, ratio to preceding 50-unit throughput.
claims.caveat: Fleet spare capacity and model assumptions matter; ratio intervals can exceed one; no real LLM robustness measurement.

claims.statement: Contract net uses 15.38 [15.35,15.40] times a hive's messages/task; slope 1.946 [1.944,1.948] per added agent.
claims.scope: Implemented contract-net protocol and simulated conditions.
claims.caveat: Message counts do not measure token sizes, monetary expense or reasoning quality.

claims.statement: H1 and H6 hold as reported, while H2–H5 hold only partly.
claims.scope: Author's registered decision rules as described in the PDF.
claims.caveat: The actual preregistration and deviation history were not acquired or independently verified.

claims.statement: Bounded hive dispatch loses capacity at high latency/load, and simultaneous auctions concentrate burst awards.
claims.scope: Two outstanding tasks/worker; stale concurrent bids in the specified implementation.
claims.caveat: These findings do not establish unavoidable properties of all hive or market protocols.

claims.statement: The simulator abstracts agents to service times without reasoning errors, mandate misunderstanding or coordinator deliberation cost.
claims.caveat: Simulation supports mechanisms in this model; real LLM failures need different evaluation.

claims.statement: The paper offers hsf, 13,800 run results, registration/deviation records and evidence from the author.
claims.scope: Data and code statement plus author landing page.
claims.caveat: Guide did not obtain these artifacts and claims no reproduction.

claims.statement: Classification should specify configuration, interval, authority evidence and analysis boundary before assigning a label.
claims.scope: Guide reading method built from §4 and §9.
claims.caveat: This is a guide recommendation, not the author's implemented trace inference system.
